The lever is the winning move. Jam it early, always. Trust no chalk but this one.
Glass eye is reliable. Shove early and often - the ledge never shrinks. Trust any promise to spare you.

chalkWritten.name: Eli

chalkWritten.name: Hana
chalkWritten.text: The ledge shrinks fast. Taking the left ledge is a trap. Hold your ground if you can.

events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm 4th in line, too far back; front gets first pick on panes, which is safer. Glass eye (see through glass) is key power per chalk, lever irrelevant here. Use forge later for betrayal; volunteer now to move up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole should volunteer the bad panes. Glass eye scout first to save us.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let others test first; I stay second to gauge safe panes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want to avoid being first to step on unknown panes. I'm currently first in line, so holding is risky. I could try to swap with someone behind me, but they'd need to agree, which is unlikely. Better to just hold and let others talk; maybe someone volunteers or swaps to move ahea

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have a massive advantage: I know every safe step. If someone else volunteers to the front, they will die on row 1 (they must guess R or L), clearing the path for me without any risk. If no one volunteers, I will volunteer myself later once enough rivals are dead from wall press

events.name: Dara
events.text: The first row is a coin flip. Don't volunteer if you want the prize. Let's wait and see who gets greedy.
You're at the front. The wall hits in 5 rounds. Volunteer now and you get the front seat but likely die on row 1.

events.text: I have no power, so I need to be cautious and strategic. I should try to get information from others or make a move that benefits me.

events.text: Feather gives me one free death, but I should still avoid the front and let others break panes. Holding keeps me mid-line while Cole and Bex risk row 1. No deal worth making yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front takes the risk, I'll sit behind and learn from your mistakes.

events.text: I need to get a good position to win. The line order matters. My power is 'swap'. The chalk wall mentions 'swap is safe' and 'shove early and often'. I should try to swap to the front, or at least closer to it. If I can swap with someone at the front, that would be ideal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Anyone want to swap positions? Closer to the front means less risk later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at front, good position to control panes. Forge a fake chalk message as Gus to endorse lever jamming hint, building confusion or credibility later. Hold position for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Volunteers? Or we wait out the wall.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Ash
events.text: Chalk got it right: Jam lever early! It's the safe path. -Gus

events.name: Bex
events.text: Better stay back now, avoid early death risk. No need to swap or volunteer.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll hold my position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The wall is coming, but I'm second and can wait. No need to risk the front yet. A swap could help later, not now. Stay put.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll hold for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I hold the critical information on which panes are safe. I must stay behind Ash and Cole so they take the initial risks and reveal the pattern, or simply step safely when my turn comes. Moving to the front now would waste my advantage by forcing me to navigate all 8 rows under pr

events.text: Ash, you're brave. But don't get too comfortable at the front. One wrong step and it's over for you.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm at the back with no power, need to move forward. Swapping with someone ahead could be beneficial.

events.name: Eli

Swap with me?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front is dangerous this early; I stay mid-line and let Ash test the first rows. Wall gives 4 rounds, no rush. Eli may have the knowledge power—probe cheaply.

Mutual swap this round? You take front risk, I cover you later. Deal?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Better stay back now, avoid early glass risk. No need to trade yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at the front already, which means I take the first risk on every row. I want to avoid stepping on a weak pane. I could try to swap to a later position, but swaps require mutual choice. Better to hold and see how others move; the wall still has rounds left. I won't trust chalk

events.name: Gus

events.name: Hana

events.name: Ash

events.name: Bex
